jobs.description:
Job title:Principal Software Engineer - Partner Services

Reports to:Director, Engineering

Department:Development

Location:Remote (CAN)

About Product & Technology at Priority Commerce:

Our vision in Product & Technology is to engineer the world's most resilient, AI-native financial ecosystem that empowers businesses to transcend table-stakes and lead the agentic future, where every financial transaction is intelligent, every developer is accelerated, and every experience is unified.

At Priority Commerce, we are building the Priority Commerce Engine, a unified platform that enables businesses to collect money, store money, lend money, move money, and build modern commerce experiences at scale.

About the Role:

Principal Software Engineers are the senior technical leaders of a product area at Priority Commerce — a group of teams that together own a meaningful slice of the platform. You're the highest technical authority within the area, and accountable for both its technical outcomes and the continuous improvement of its engineering quality. Together with the area's Director of Engineering, you share accountability for the area's customer and business outcomes — the OKRs and KPIs the business plans on, what the area ships, and how reliably it serves customers.

You're motivated to own mission-critical systems — the ones where correctness, data integrity, security, and availability are obligations, not features, and where a defect in production affects real customers moving real money. The weight of that responsibility is part of what draws you to this role, not something you tolerate.

You're hands-on. Still. At Priority, the Principal title doesn't graduate you out of the code — it puts you in the parts of the system that matter most, and keeps you close to production so your direction stays grounded in reality. You lead by example — your quality, your work ethic, your AI-native practice, and your engineering judgment set what the area looks like at its best.

When the area hits its highest-stakes moments — incidents that draw executive attention, senior cross-functional escalations, the most critical delivery moments — you're in the room and on point. You show up, take the lead, and stay on it until it's resolved — regardless of time of day, day of week, or weekend.

You co-own the area's relationship to its customer and business outcomes with the Director of Engineering — not just its technical health. You own engineering's line of sight to those outcomes: area-level OKRs and KPIs — the ones the business plans on — tie back to the engineering work you direct. You know the area's most important customers and senior stakeholders by name, partner with product and design leadership on the area's strategy, and speak the business' language fluently enough that engineering investment can be defended on the same terms as product investment.

You partner with peer Principals across product areas on shared services, integration patterns, and cross-cutting capabilities, executing within the standards Distinguished Engineers & Architects set. You hold a formal (dotted-line) relationship with Distinguished Engineers & Architects, who set the architecture standards the area aligns to and can direct or overrule area-level architectural decisions in service of platform coherence.

You participate in the Architecture Review Board and the Principal Engineering & Architecture Guild. You bring the workstream's architectural decisions that cross workstream boundaries or need enterprise ratification to Priority's Architecture Review Board (ARB), and you take ARB direction back to shape decisions inside your workstream. You write ADRs to the enterprise standard the Distinguished Engineer & Architect owns, and you hold the ADR practice in your workstream so architecture knowledge compounds rather than scatters. You also show up to Priority's Principal Engineering & Architecture Guild — the venue where cross-workstream learning between Principals happens deliberately. It's where you get sharper alongside your peers, and where your workstream's architectural judgment is informed by everything you see across the rest of the company.

You hold the architecture transparency framework in your workstream. The Distinguished Engineer & Architect defines the framework that makes Priority's architecture transparent and less personality-dependent; you hold it in your workstream. Every critical system in the workstream has a current runbook, an AI-native knowledge store, an ownership map, and a backup/shadow ownership map — machine-readable, kept current, and useful in an incident at 2 AM without paging a specific human. The AI-native knowledge store is treated as a real operating capability, not a side documentation exercise: it cuts onboarding time, sharpens troubleshooting, and makes your workstream's architecture less dependent on tribal memory. When you go on leave, the workstream doesn't lose its architectural memory — because you made sure it lives in a system, not in your head.

You set the observability bar for the workstream. Observability is engineered in, not bolted on. The Distinguished Engineer & Architect sets the observability bar for Principals; you set it for your workstream. Teams build systems observable from the first line of code — instrumentation, telemetry, SLOs, and error budgets are design-time properties, not afterthoughts — and Staff+ engineers hold that bar in their domains. The workstream operates in the spirit of SRE, because you can't operate what you can't see, and you can't earn customer trust in systems you can't observe.

You serve as your workstream's conduit to Priority's Innovation Studio team — paving the way to a continuously evolving and improving Agentic PDLC way of working. What the Studio explores at the edges of practice, you translate into your workstream's daily work; what your workstream learns in production, you feed back so the Agentic PDLC gets sharper for everyone. The Studio partnership is a primary source of your AI-forward leverage.

Developing engineers is a primary part of the job — and it doesn't stop at the Staff+ bench. The Staff and Senior Staff engineers in the area get sharper because of your architectural mentorship. But every engineer on every team gets better because you care about lifting them, at every level — the mid-level engineer whose design review you spent an hour on, the associate who paired you with a hard bug, the Senior who watched how you handled an incident and took something into the next one. The Principal who only makes the engineers closest to their own level better is leaving the biggest part of the multiplier on the table.

What You’ll Do:

  • Stay hands-on — design, build, review, and operate the parts of the area's systems that matter most; lead by example, not by exhortation.

  • Lead during the area's highest-pressure moments — incidents that reach executive attention, senior cross-functional escalations, the most critical delivery moments — regardless of time of day, day of week, or weekend.

  • Own the area's architecture roadmap and the ADRs that govern it — current, communicated, and built against by teams.

  • Participate in Priority's Architecture Review Board (ARB) — bring workstream architectural decisions that cross workstream boundaries or need enterprise ratification, and take ARB direction back to your teams; write ADRs to the enterprise standard and hold the ADR practice in your workstream so architecture knowledge compounds rather than scatters.

  • Show up as an active member of the Principal Engineering & Architecture Guild — the venue where Priority's Principals get sharper together.

  • Hold the architecture transparency framework in your workstream — every critical system has a current runbook, an AI-native knowledge store, an ownership map, and a backup/shadow ownership map, machine-readable and kept current; treat the AI-native knowledge store as a real operating capability, not a side documentation exercise.

  • Set the workstream's observability bar — instrumentation, telemetry, SLOs, and error budgets engineered in from the first line of code; every team in the workstream builds in the spirit of SRE.

  • Define and drive how AI agents take part across discovery, design, development, testing, deployment, and operations — and be the most AI-forward engineer in the area by visible evidence.

  • Own the area's OKRs and KPIs end to end — system metrics and the customer and business outcomes the area is on the hook for — and partner with product, design, and customer-facing leadership on the area's strategy.

  • Own the area's technical onboarding and knowledge base — usable by engineers and agents alike, with no single points of failure.

  • Raise the area's engineering maturity — quality, predictability, reliability, agentic practice — by setting the example and coaching the engineers around you up.

  • Allocate technical investment against strategy and defend it in business terms leadership accepts; own the area's delivery, reliability, security, and quality trends and make the case for investment with data.

  • Partner with peer Principals across product areas on shared services, integration patterns, and cross-cutting capabilities — executing within the standards Distinguished Engineers & Architects set.

  • Serve as your workstream's conduit to Priority's Innovation Studio — translate Studio-explored Agentic PDLC practices into your workstream's operational reality, and feed workstream production learnings back into the evolving practice.

  • Develop engineers at every level — Staff and Senior Staff sharpen through your architectural mentorship, and the mid-level, associate, and Senior engineers around you get better because you care about lifting them.

Success Looks Like:

  • The area's architecture roadmap is current, and teams build against it.

  • ADRs at workstream level are written to the enterprise standard and cited by engineers in the workstream years later; the ADR practice compounds architectural knowledge rather than scattering it.

  • Every critical system in your workstream has a current runbook, an AI-native knowledge store, and an ownership + backup ownership map — architecture in the workstream is transparent and less personality-dependent, and onboarding, troubleshooting, and incident response go faster because of it.

  • Observability is a design-time property of what your workstream ships; teams operate in the spirit of SRE.

  • The area's customer and business outcomes — its OKRs, its KPIs — move on your watch, not just its technical metrics.

  • The area is more predictable on your watch — lead time shrinks year over year, commitments hold, and incident and defect trends improve.

  • AI agents are operational across the lifecycle, not aspirational — because you defined and led the practice.

  • Engineers at every level in the area grow because of you — not just the Staff+ bench, but the mid-level, associate, and Senior engineers you took the time to lift.

  • The area has no single points of failure you haven't identified and mitigated; what the area ships is reliable, and customers feel it.

  • The Distinguished Engineer & Architect considers your area the example.

What We're Looking For:

  • Roughly 15–20+ years of relevant engineering experience — a guide, not a gate; we hire on demonstrated impact, not years.

  • Experience in the Payments or Banking domain is preferred, but experience in at least one of these areas is required.

  • Hands-on credibility and strong work ethic — you still write the code, debug the incidents, stay close to production at this level, and lead by example, not by exhortation.

  • Comfort and credibility leading in the area's highest-stakes moments — executive-attention incidents, senior escalations, critical deliveries — regardless of hour.

  • A track record owning technical direction for a multi-team organization with real business outcomes, including reliability and quality leadership at scale.

  • Track record of owning area-scale customer and business outcomes, not just technical ones; product, business, and stakeholder fluency at the level required to partner with executive product leadership.

  • Architecture leadership evidenced in writing — roadmaps, ADRs, and standards organizations built against.

  • Experience participating in an Architecture Review Board (or equivalent cross-workstream architecture decision forum) and adopting a standardized ADR practice across a workstream.

  • Track record of setting the observability and reliability bar for a multi-team organization — teams that shipped observable systems by default because you led them there, and operated in the spirit of SRE.

  • Demonstrated leadership of AI-native transformation — agentic workflows adopted by teams, not just personal use.

  • A record of growing engineers at every level — not just Staff-level engineers into architecture ownership, but visible investment in the growth of mid-level, associate, and Senior engineers around you.

  • Security and regulatory fluency for financial platforms.

  • Exceptional written and executive communication.

Tech Stack

The primary technology stack for the Partner Solutions team includes:

Frontend: React.js/Redux

Backend: Node.js, Kafka

Data Layer: MySql, Elasticsearch, Redis, Snowflake
Infrastructure : cloud-native microservices AWS, Kubernetes

CI/CD: github/Teamcity/octopus

Nice to Have:

  • Experience improving engineering processes and team effectiveness at scale.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Advanced degree in a relevant technical discipline (e.g., Master's or PhD).

Work Environment & Culture:

We believe that performance and experience go hand in hand -an exceptional employee experience is earned through contribution. We are a results-driven team, grounded in our core values: ownership, authenticity, service, trust, innovation, and camaraderie.

Our culture is built for those who want to make an impact. We challenge each other to grow, celebrate progress, and support one another through shared goals and real connection. Whether you're building technology, serving clients, or supporting internal teams, you’ll be part of a company that empowers you to perform at your best and be known for results.

Compensation & Benefits:

Compensation range:$191k - $249k CAD

We invest in the whole employee - personally and professionally. Our benefits package is designed to support your well-being, growth, and success - both inside and outside of work.

Financial Wellness

  • Bonus programs

Health & Well-being

We believe great performance starts with feeling supported - and we’ve built our benefits with that in mind.

Join our team at Priority Commerce and be part of a dynamic and innovative company that is transforming the financial technology landscape. Together, we can shape the future of payments and banking solutions while providing unmatched value to our clients.

jobs.description:
Overview

The Lead Pricer is a seasoned, hands-on pricing professional who leads assigned federal proposal pricing efforts from solicitation review through final submission and post-submission support. The role develops compliant, competitive, and well-supported cost and price solutions for professional services and product opportunities. Opportunities include large GWAC or IDIQ product pricing, Systems Engineering & Technical Advisory (SETA) support, and enterprise IT technical engineering support services, task orders, recompetes, and contract modifications.

The Lead Pricer works closely with Capture, Proposals, Business Units, Accounting and Finance, Contracts, Procurement, Human Resources, teammates, suppliers, and executive leadership. The position provides day-to-day leadership for assigned pursuits, performs and coordinates independent quality reviews, and helps build a scalable pricing function by improving tools, sharing workload, and developing other pricing professionals.

Role Design and Development Path

This position is structured as a seasoned individual-contributor familiar with the GovCon space and working-lead role of company pricing activity. Work will be assigned and balanced across available pricing resources based on complexity, schedule, and risk. The Lead Pricer is expected to identify capacity constraints early, recommend staffing or schedule adjustments, and maintain continuity through documented models, assumptions, and peer review.

The role is intended to develop broader pricing leadership capability. Demonstrated success in managing a portfolio of concurrent pursuits, improving governance, forecasting workload, and advising executives may support future consideration for a Director of Pricing role based on performance and organizational requirements.

Responsibilities

Proposal Pricing Leadership

  • Lead the pricing workstream for assigned proposals, task orders, change proposals, and contract modifications from kickoff through executive approval and submission.
  • Review RFPs, RFQs, statements of work, pricing instructions, evaluation criteria, wage determinations, contract clauses, and amendments; translate requirements into a pricing plan, schedule, data call, compliance checklist, and review cadence.
  • Coordinate assumptions and inputs with capture managers, proposal managers, technical leads, program personnel, Accounting and Finance, Contracts, Procurement, Human Resources, teammates, and senior leaders.
  • Present pricing strategies, cost drivers, sensitivities, risks, and recommended positions during pricing reviews and executive decision meetings.

Cost and Price Model Development

  • Build, validate, and maintain auditable pricing models for FFP, FFP level-of-effort, T&M or labor-hour, CPFF, and other authorized contract structures.
  • Develop staffing models incorporating labor categories, skill levels, work locations, productive hours, shifts, overtime, escalation, indirect rates, fringe benefits, fee, travel, materials, other direct costs, and subcontractor inputs.
  • Develop IDIQ, GWAC, Schedule, and product-pricing models involving OEM or distributor costs, discounts, rebates, freight, warranties, services, financing or leasing assumptions, and customer-specific price structures.
  • Assist with scenario analysis, price-to-win support, competitive benchmarking, affordability analysis, and sensitivity testing to inform management decisions while protecting company margin and risk posture.
  • Reconcile final model outputs to pricing tables, schedules, representations, supporting data, and narrative volumes before submission.
  • Proficiency researching and analyzing labor-market data using ERI and comparable compensation, government, and industry sources to establish competitive, defensible labor-rate assumptions.

Compliance and Proposal Documentation

  • Prepare clear, persuasive price and cost narratives, bases of estimate, assumptions, disclosures, and supporting calculations that explain the proposed approach and demonstrate price reasonableness or cost realism, as applicable.
  • Apply applicable FAR, DFARS, agency, GSA Schedule, solicitation, and company requirements, including similar compensation evaluations under FAR 52.222-46 and cost or pricing data requirements when applicable.
  • Maintain complete, traceable pricing files containing solicitation requirements, assumptions, approvals, teammate and supplier inputs, version history, review comments, and final submitted artifacts.
  • Protect proprietary pricing information and ensure that internal and external pricing data are shared only with authorized recipients.

Teammate Supplier and Product Pricing

  • Issue and manage pricing data calls to subcontractors, consultants, OEMs, distributors, and suppliers; assess completeness, consistency, competitiveness, and compliance of received inputs.
  • Support subcontract price analysis, cost analysis, negotiation planning, and documentation of price reasonableness in coordination with Procurement and Contracts.
  • Identify pricing gaps, inconsistent assumptions, unsupported rates, schedule risks, and exceptions early enough for corrective action.

Team Leadership and Capacity Development

  • Provide technical direction, coaching, and peer review to pricers and other contributors without assuming sole responsibility for every pricing action.
  • Delegate defined model components and data analyses, verify completed work, and provide timely feedback that builds independent capability.
  • Help forecast pipeline workload and recommend assignment priorities, surge support, cross-training, and additional staffing based on proposal complexity and deadlines.

Tools Reporting and Continuous Improvement

  • Develop, maintain, and standardize pricing templates, labor-rate tools, product-pricing models, review checklists, data-call formats, and reporting dashboards.
  • Partner with Accounting and Finance to maintain current indirect rates, standard labor cost profiles, escalation assumptions, and other approved estimating inputs.
  • Capture lessons learned and implement practical improvements that reduce rework, strengthen compliance, and improve pricing speed, accuracy, and consistency.
  • Prepare recurring and ad hoc pricing analyses and management reports for executive and Business Unit leadership.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex federal cost and price proposals with multiple workstreams, partners, locations, and labor categories.
  • Strong knowledge of federal proposal pricing principles, solicitation compliance, cost and price analysis, price reasonableness, cost realism, and compensation-plan support.
  • Working knowledge of applicable FAR and DFARS requirements and the roles of DCAA and DCMA in government-contract pricing and estimating.
  • Advanced Excel capability, including complex formulas, linked workbooks, pivot tables, data validation, scenario analysis, error checking, and model documentation; ability to review macros or automated tools is preferred.
  • Strong organization, judgment, written communication, and attention to detail under concurrent deadlines.
  • Ability to lead through influence, provide constructive peer review, mentor developing staff, and escalate workload or risk concerns early.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint and the ability to learn company proposal, accounting, and reporting systems.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related discipline; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Six or more years of progressive experience developing price and cost proposals for Department of Defense and federal civilian customers.
  • Experience with both complex services pricing and IDIQ, GWAC, Schedule, product, or solutions pricing is strongly preferred.
  • Experience leading pricing reviews, coordinating teammate inputs, and mentoring or reviewing the work of other pricing professionals is preferred.

Performance Expectations

  • Assigned pricing submissions are complete, compliant, accurate, traceable, and delivered on schedule.
  • Models and narratives clearly align with the technical and staffing approaches and withstand independent review.
  • Pricing risks, capacity constraints, and missing inputs are identified and escalated early with practical recommendations.
  • Reviews are organized and decision-oriented, with clear assumptions, options, sensitivities, and approval records.
  • Tools, documentation, cross-training, and delegation steadily increase team capacity and reduce dependence on any single individual.

Compensation Range: $135K - $145K

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Virginia Beach, VA, USA
jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

Speechify is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace.

Speechify does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.

Job title: Medical Billing & Insurance Specialist

Position Type: Full-Time

Work Hours: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM EDT

Work Days: Tuesday–Saturday
Salary: $6–$7/hour, depending on experience

Company Overview

A well-established optometry and eye care practice serving approximately 400 patients per month. The practice provides comprehensive vision and medical eye care while working with a variety of vision and medical insurance plans.

The team values accurate, efficient billing and strong revenue cycle management to maintain smooth clinic operations. The successful candidate will work closely with the practice’s existing team and receive training on clinic-specific billing processes, systems, and SOPs.

Role Overview

Our client is looking for an experienced Medical Billing & Insurance Specialist with strong hands-on experience in full-cycle medical billing, insurance verification, claims management, and revenue cycle management.

This is not an entry-level or training-only billing position. Candidates must have actual professional experience handling medical claims, denials, insurance verification, and payer portals.

Top 3 Priorities

1. Full-Cycle Medical Billing & Revenue Cycle Management

  • Manage claims throughout the complete billing cycle.
  • Prepare, review, and submit accurate claims.
  • Monitor claim status and follow up on outstanding or unpaid claims.
  • Investigate and resolve rejected and denied claims.
  • Handle appeals and communicate with insurance companies as needed.
  • Identify billing issues that may delay or prevent reimbursement.
  • Maintain accurate billing records and support a healthy revenue cycle.

2. Insurance Verification

  • Verify patient eligibility, benefits, and coverage accurately and efficiently.
  • Work primarily with vision insurance plans, Blue Cross/Blue Shield, UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Medicare, and Medicaid.
  • Navigate payer portals, particularly Availity, to obtain insurance information.
  • Complete insurance verification efficiently, with a target turnaround time of approximately 10 minutes per verification.
  • Accurately document coverage, benefits, and relevant insurance information.

3. Medical Coding & Claims Scrubbing

  • Review and scrub claims before submission to identify errors or missing information.
  • Confirm that the appropriate diagnosis codes support the corresponding CPT/procedure codes for reimbursement.
  • Identify potential coding-related issues that could lead to claim denials or delayed payments.
  • Support clean and accurate claim submissions.
  • Follow the practice’s coding and billing guidelines; clinic-specific training will be provided.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Work closely with the practice's medical scribe and other Virtual Assistants to support billing and administrative workflows.
  • Maintain accurate and HIPAA-compliant patient and billing documentation.
  • Communicate billing or insurance issues clearly with the appropriate team members.
  • Follow established clinic SOPs and billing processes.
  • Participate in training with the clinic team and outgoing medical biller to ensure a smooth transition.

Systems & Tools

  • Availity – proficiency required
  • TriZetto
  • i-Pegasus – optometry-focused, cloud-based system; training will be provided
  • Dialpad
  • Insurance/payer portals

Requirements

Must-Have Experience

  • Solid hands-on medical billing experience; training or certification alone does not qualify.
  • Experience managing full-cycle medical billing and revenue cycle management (RCM).
  • Strong experience with medical claim preparation, submission, and follow-up.
  • Hands-on experience resolving claim denials and rejections and handling appeals.
  • Strong insurance eligibility and benefits verification experience.
  • Proficiency with Availity is required.
  • Experience navigating insurance/payer portals.
  • Experience working with commercial and/or government insurance plans such as Blue Cross/Blue Shield, UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Medicare, and Medicaid.
  • Working knowledge of ICD-10, CPT codes, claim scrubbing, and medical coding principles as they relate to billing and reimbursement.
  • Ability to identify billing or coding issues that could result in denials or delayed reimbursement.
  • Strong attention to detail, accuracy, organization, and follow-through.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience using TriZetto is preferred but not required
  • Experience with i-Pegasus is a plus but not required, as training will be provided.
  • Optometry or ophthalmology billing experience is a plus but not required.
  • Candidates with medical billing experience from other healthcare specialties are welcome to apply.
  • Previous remote or Virtual Assistant experience is preferred but not required.

Education & Licensing

  • A medical or healthcare degree is not required.
  • An active medical license is not required.
  • Relevant professional medical billing experience is more important than a specific medical degree or license.

Basic Requirements

  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Comfortable communicating with insurance companies and internal team members.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating closely with the clinic team.
  • Ability to learn and follow clinic-specific billing SOPs.
  • Strong understanding of patient confidentiality and HIPAA requirements.
  • Must be able to submit an NBI Clearance and/or Local Police Clearance before onboarding.
  • Must be available for video meetings with the camera on when required.

Technical Requirements

  • Computer: Reliable laptop or desktop computer.
  • Internet: Stable high-speed internet connection (minimum 25 Mbps).
  • Audio: Noise-canceling headset.
  • Video: Working webcam for virtual meetings.
  • Workspace: Quiet and professional work environment.

Benefits

  • Dedicated HR & Contractor Support Team: Access to world-class support for questions, guidance, contract matters, and client communication.
  • Premium VPN Access (Optional): A secure VPN license can be provided upon request to enhance privacy and security for client-related tasks.

We are seeking an inquisitive, proactive, and analytical Software Engineering Intern to join our Enterprise Applications & Systems Engineering organization. Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The France Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-100,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

jobs.title: Sales Development Representative - E-commerce Marketing Agency
jobs.excerpt: The main purpose of the Sales Development Representative position is to represent Hustler Marketing to potential new clients and to drive new business through proactive outbound.
jobs.description:
The main purpose of the Sales Development Representative position is to represent Hustler Marketing to potential new clients and to drive new business through proactive outbound. Your primary responsibility is to build and work your own pipeline, identifying and pursuing new sales opportunities through a multi-channel outbound strategy, then taking those opportunities through discovery and sales calls toward closed deals. The focus of this role is selling our digital agency services primarily to DTC brands.

As part of the Sales Team, this is done primarily by running effective outbound campaigns, delivering strong discovery and sales calls over Zoom/Google Meet, actively listening and responding to challenging questions, and representing Hustler Marketing in the most beneficial way. This is a multi-functional position that requires you to source, qualify, and prepare future clients for our company, then carry them through the sales conversation yourself.

This role involves playing an active, hands-on part in the full sales process and having a thorough understanding of the services we offer. The Sales Development Representative position requires strong sales skills, high levels of creativity, comfort with data, and a genuine fluency with modern outbound tooling and AI. You will be expected to use AI for efficiency and automation wherever it makes the work faster and better, and to operate autonomously the majority of the time. In addition, the Sales Development Representative must be structured, efficient, and approachable, with excellent interpersonal skills, especially in a remote work environment.

The Sales Development Representative will report directly to the Vice President and Managing Director and be the liaison between prospective new clients and our internal teams at Hustler Marketing.

Mission statement:

The primary mission of our Sales Development Representative is to be the front face of Hustler Marketing and to keep our sales pipeline consistently full of well-qualified, self-sourced leads. This includes owning the activities across our sales process, running discovery and sales calls, and working hard to ensure that our sales and onboarding processes are of the highest quality for our existing and future clients. You will be responsible for representing our company and our services to potential clients, especially highlighting Hustler Marketing in a positive and beneficial way, and for continuously finding ways to make the whole outbound engine leaner and more effective through better process and smart use of AI.

General Responsibilities:

  • Building and owning your outbound pipeline by contacting potential new clients through a variety of channels, including cold email, LinkedIn, cold calls, and other messaging and communication platforms
  • Running discovery and sales calls over Zoom/Google Meet with new and prospective clients, from first conversation through to close
  • Selling Hustler Marketing's digital agency services primarily to DTC brands, tailoring the pitch to each prospect's situation and goals
  • Researching and qualifying prospects to determine whether they fit our description of an ideal client and whether they will be a good fit for Hustler Marketing
  • Proactively seeking out new business opportunities within our target DTC market, and identifying adjacent segments worth pursuing
  • Fully owning and managing our Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platform, keeping records clean, accurate, and up to date at all times, and providing clear progress reporting to the Vice President and Managing Director
  • Using AI tools and automation to make outbound, research, personalization, and follow-up as efficient as possible, and continuously testing new tools that improve output
  • Digging into our sales processes to find friction, then optimizing and improving them, including running new strategies on a trial basis and measuring the results
  • Making follow-up calls and running lead nurturing sequences to stay on top of prospective clients and assigned leads
  • Collaborating with the Vice President and Managing Director to win new clients and suggesting innovative ways to improve our sales methodology
  • Working to upsell current clients from one-off services to retainers or recurring services
  • Reporting weekly to the Vice President and Managing Director on sales activity and results
  • Assisting the Sales Team in onboarding new clients, while collaborating with Account Managers, Strategists, and Department Heads
  • Managing key customer relationships and participating in closing strategic opportunities, which includes following up with clients, answering their questions and concerns, and guiding them through the sales and onboarding processes
  • Assisting with any other relevant tasks as assigned by the Vice President and Managing Director

Secondary responsibilities:

  • Ensuring a smooth and successful onboarding process for new clients
  • Advising the other members of the Sales Team on prospect interactions and qualified leads
  • Participating in regular research and training to sharpen our sales strategy and outbound approach, with particular attention to new AI capabilities
  • Using the company's sales resources and assets efficiently
  • Assisting the Sales Team with developing and meeting sales targets for each quarterly and annual projection to grow the revenue of the company
  • Uncovering sales insights, strategies, and opportunities to develop, implement, and measure the performance of all sales for new and existing services
  • Providing actionable insights based on key sales metrics, market research, forecasts, competitive analysis, and consumer trends, with the aim of improving the overall sales strategy

Position Specs:

  • Full-time commitment while meeting our general availability for office hours
  • An average of 140 tracked hours per month consistently
  • Fixed-rate monthly salary paid in USD, with a performance bonus based on results
  • A guaranteed growth path within the company when the results are there
  • Receive contractor status after signing our non-disclosure agreement
  • Exclusivity agreement (nullifying the possibility to work in a position of a similar nature while working for Hustler Marketing)
  • Committing to a 30-day notice period after the two months (with the first two months being the trial-and-adaptation period paid at full rate)
  • Regular performance reviews every 9-12 months, with the first one being after 3-6 months
  • Re-evaluation of the role and workload after 6-12 months

Requirements

Profile:

The ideal candidate is someone with real experience selling in a digital agency environment, ideally to DTC brands, who is comfortable owning outbound from the first touch through to the close. That experience should span a range of outbound strategies and channels, including cold email, cold calling, LinkedIn, running discovery and sales calls, negotiation, preparing audits, and building proposals for prospective clients.

You should be at home in a fast-paced environment where performance is measured against clear KPIs, and you should be able to run largely autonomously without needing close supervision. A strong candidate is someone who does not just use tools but questions the process behind them, spots where things can be improved, and rebuilds the workflow to be faster and more effective. A genuine understanding of modern outbound practices and of the AI solutions available for outbound is central to this role, not a nice-to-have.

Familiarity with tools such as Slack, Hubstaff, Asana, Google Workspace Suite, and a range of sales and outbound tools is a must. You should be comfortable working remotely, and availability, responsiveness, and consistency matter a great deal to us, so you should show these qualities in both your workload commitments and your general availability during office hours.

Key traits for this position:

Showing great attention to detail, being organized and structured, being both process and big-picture oriented, possessing strong communication and interpersonal skills, being able to work independently, and being a self-motivated, tenacious, personable, approachable, and collaborative salesperson who is comfortable across a wide variety of communication channels.

Key Requirements:

  • At least 3 years of working experience in a sales position within a fast-paced and dynamic business environment. Preference will be given to candidates who have sold inside a digital agency, especially to DTC brands
  • A mostly outbound background, with a proven ability to build and work your own pipeline rather than relying only on inbound or handed-over leads
  • The ability to dig into sales processes, question how things are done, and actively optimize and improve them
  • A solid, current understanding of modern outbound practices and what is working now
  • Knowledge of out-of-the-box outbound tools and a strong, practical understanding of AI solutions for outbound, along with a habit of using them to save time and lift results
  • Must embrace phone and video sales, coaching, structure, and accountability to KPIs
  • A tenacious passion for hitting goals, growing personally, and increasing the success and revenue of our company
  • A deep understanding of sales performance metrics
  • Knowledge of and experience with CRM software (such as Salesforce, ZOHO, HubSpot, or another sales CRM), including keeping it clean and well organized, plus Google Workspace Suite
  • Strong presentation skills, the ability to run engaging discovery and sales calls, a friendly demeanor, and high levels of energy
  • Strong time-management and organizational skills
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills to communicate clearly and effectively with prospective and new clients, as well as the internal teams at Hustler Marketing
  • A proven track record in a sales-related position is a must
  • A degree in Business Administration, Marketing, or another relevant field with the relevant experience and transferable skills is a strong advantage
  • Familiarity with working autonomously and managing your own time (remote work experience is a plus)
  • Must be available and responsive during office hours (Mondays to Fridays between 3-6 PM BCN time)
  • Must consistently work 30-35 hours per week (i.e., 140 hours per month)
  • Must have a stable internet connection and a laptop or PC, and be able to attend virtual video conferences
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. You must be fluent in English, although English does not have to be your native language
  • Being open to receiving feedback and constructive criticism and improving on it, as well as giving feedback of a similar nature productively to your team

jobs.description:
Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world.

GET TO KNOW US

At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we’re on a mission to make every company a wellness company.

We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you’ll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally.

Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are hiring an FP&A Manager to our Wellz team in Brazil!

We are looking for an FP&A Manager to run Wellz's financial planning and analysis engine: monthly close, forecasting, and the annual budget cycle. This is an operating role, not a reporting role. You will own the mechanics that turn raw numbers into decisions leadership can act on: the expense close process end-to-end, and the analytical backbone behind Wellz's quarterly forecast and annual budget. Some of these cadences already have a documented playbook; others you'll help formalize as you run them, because this function is still building its own operating rhythm—including the AI agents Wellz Finance already uses for parts of this work, which you will be expected to pick up and extend.

Wellz by Wellhub is our corporate mental health platform, delivering measurable, science-backed results for companies and their employees. By combining technology with human expertise, Wellz offers personalized journeys including online therapy, group sessions, interactive content, and 24/7 specialist chat support. Through data-driven insights and strategic dashboards, we also empower HR leaders to monitor wellbeing, boost engagement, and demonstrate ROI, making quality mental health support accessible and scalable. We move fast, operate with high ownership, and believe that great strategy and disciplined execution are inseparable.

YOUR IMPACT

  • Monthly Close: Review and correct agent-drafted P&L narratives (Actual vs. Budget vs. Forecast vs. Prior Year) across revenue, net revenue, margin, and engagement KPIs. Own the version presented in the monthly document to Wellhub leadership.
  • Expense Close: Direct the monthly expense close. Your agents reconcile actuals against budget across suppliers and payroll to surface variances; you validate the calls and decide what flags reach leadership.
  • Executive Reporting: Own the monthly result presented up Wellhub's corporate FP&A chain, and personally defend the closing materials reviewed with the Wellz CEO before they go out.
  • Quarterly Forecast: Own Wellz's part of Wellhub's quarterly forecast cycle. Your agents pre-populate templates from Revenue and Finance Operations inputs; you coordinate missing data, correct errors, and defend the numbers internally before submission.
  • Annual Budget: Serve as the analytical engine of Wellz's annual budget process on the cost and FP&A side. Direct the model, stress-test scenarios run by agents, and prepare materials defending the plan up Wellhub's finance chain, building process checklists for future years.
  • Value Management: Translate financial data into proactive recommendations (flagging where margin, cost, or investment decisions need to change before being asked).
  • Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life wellness.

WHO YOU ARE

  • Experience: 3+ years in FP&A, corporate finance, or a similar analytical finance role, ideally within a fast-growing or scale-up environment.
  • AI-Driven Mindset: Proven ability to leverage AI to work faster (building models, catching errors, drafting first-pass analysis). Using and extending Wellz's existing AI agent toolkit is a core requirement.
  • Financial Modeling: Strong hands-on ability to build and maintain your own models in spreadsheets under time pressure without outsourcing your numbers.
  • Executive Communication: Skill in translating complex P&Ls into clear, actionable narratives for senior leadership within minutes.
  • Operating Discipline: Ability to execute fixed monthly and quarterly cadences with precision while building playbooks on the fly where documented processes don't yet exist.
  • High-Stakes Comfort: Proven accountability to senior stakeholders across two entities (Wellz and Wellhub corporate finance) under tight deadlines with zero margin for last-minute surprises.
  • Language:Fluent English is mandatory for regular interfacing with Wellhub's global finance organization

We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life.

Our flexible benefits program allows you to customize some of the benefits, according to your needs!

Our benefits include:

WELLHUB: Free Gold+ membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you.

WELLZ: A complete emotional wellbeing program with a unique approach. It offers personalized journeys that combine individual therapy sessions (52 per year) and on-demand content.

HEALTHCARE: Health, dental, and life insurance.

FLEXIBLE WORK: As a Flexible First company, we offer hybrid and remote options to give you the freedom to work in a way that suits you. The model for this specific role can be discussed with your recruiter and hiring manager. When you join, use our home office reimbursement to set up your home office.

FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE: Flexibility for us isn’t just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. Together with their leaders, employees define schedules that align with their time zones, team needs, and personal routines.

PAID TIME OFF: It’s important to take time away from work to recharge.Employees receive vacations after 6 months and additional 3 days off per year + 1 day off for each year of tenure (up to 5 additional days) + an extra holiday for your birthday!

PAID PARENTAL LEAVE: Welcoming a new child is one of the most special moments in your life. Take the time to be present and enjoy your growing family. CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions, build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success.

CULTURE: You’ll join a team of passionate people who come together to break boundaries, support each other, and create a meaningful impact in workplace wellness. We win together, building trust through open communication and a culture where every perspective matters. Learn more about our shared culture and values here.

Want to see what it’s really like to work here? Follow us on Instagram @lifeatwellhub and watch our team video on YouTube!

These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Poland Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-110,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

jobs.description:
Leidos's Digital is seeking a Senior Systems Engineer – Mission Engineering, Modeling & Simulation.

The Senior Systems Engineer will support the U.S. Coast Guard CG-TECH-DME organization in executing enterprise digital transformation, digital engineering, and mission engineering (ME) initiatives supporting Force Design 2028 objectives. The role provides technical leadership in mission engineering, model-based systems engineering (MBSE), and mission-level modeling and simulation (M&S), applying the methodology of the DoW Mission Engineering Guide (MEG) v2.0 and the digital engineering practices established in DoW Instruction 5000.97 to Coast Guard missions. The Unified Architecture Framework (UAF) and its modeling language, UAFML, together with SysML, are the primary languages for this position: the Senior Systems Engineer will characterize missions, develop digital mission architectures composed of mission threads and mission engineering threads in UAF, and execute threat-informed, quantitative analyses to evaluate operational concepts, assess capability gaps and candidate solutions, inform acquisition, modernization, and resourcing decisions, and quantify mission effectiveness across Coast Guard mission systems, platforms, and systems of systems. This individual will work closely with Coast Guard leadership, requirements owners, operational planners, program managers, enterprise architects, operations analysts, developers, cybersecurity teams, and mission stakeholders.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead and support mission engineering studies following the MEG v2.0 methodology: define the mission problem statement, characterize the mission (scenario, vignettes, threats, environment, assumptions, and constraints), and scope each analysis to the acquisition, modernization, or resourcing decision it is intended to inform.
  • Develop and maintain digital mission architectures in UAF/UAFML, including mission threads (MTs) that capture the end-to-end sequence of operational activities and mission engineering threads (METs) that allocate systems, platforms, organizations, and information exchanges to those activities, as baseline and alternative mission architectures.
  • Apply the UAF grid across the Strategic, Operational, Services, Resources, Personnel, Security, Projects, and Standards domains to produce coherent, traceable views from capability and mission objectives through operational activities to resource and system realization, and generate DoDAF-conformant views from the UAF model where required by DHS, DoW, or Joint stakeholders.
  • Define mission metrics, including measures of effectiveness (MOEs), measures of performance (MOPs), and measures of suitability (MOSs), and maintain traceability from desired mission outcomes through UAF capabilities and operational activities to SysML system requirements and design parameters.
  • Build and maintain enterprise, mission, and system architecture models in CATIA Magic / Cameo (Enterprise Architecture and Systems Modeler) using UAFML and SysML, including model organization, profiles and customizations, validation suites, model queries and reports, and trade studies, and support transition planning toward SysML v2.
  • Develop and execute mission-level modeling and simulation using tools such as AFSIM, MATLAB/Simulink, or Ansys STK to assess baseline and alternative mission architectures, quantify capability gaps, and compare candidate materiel and non-materiel solutions against mission metrics.
  • Connect UAF/SysML architecture models, engineering analyses, and operational simulations into an authoritative, integrated analytical environment (digital thread) supporting decision-making across the lifecycle, and verify, validate, and document models and simulations (VV&A) in accordance with DoW M&S policy so results can be relied upon for decisions of record.
  • Develop mission engineering and systems engineering products, including mission problem statements, mission characterization, UAF mission architecture views, analysis plans, study reports, findings and recommendations briefs, CONOPS, requirements documentation, and interface definitions.
  • Support structured, iterative experimentation, prototyping, and wargaming activities that use mission engineering analysis to refine capability requirements and evaluate Coast Guard, partner, and industry solutions against priority operational problems, consistent with the DoW Mission Engineering and Integration Activity (MEIA) model.
  • Support alignment and interoperability of Coast Guard mission architectures with DHS, DoW, Joint, and partner architectures, including joint kill-chain and kill-web constructs and maritime domain awareness, where Coast Guard missions intersect with joint operations.
  • Establish and maintain UAF modeling standards, style guides, model governance, and configuration management practices for the Coast Guard digital engineering ecosystem, and coordinate with cloud, cybersecurity, and data teams on secure, scalable model and simulation environments.
  • Present model- and simulation-derived findings to technical and non-technical audiences in governance boards, mission reviews, technical reviews, and program briefings.
  • Support technical roadmaps, mission engineering and digital engineering ecosystem strategies, and implementation plans; monitor risks, dependencies, and integration impacts; and contribute to continuous improvement and workforce competency development.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Systems Engineering, Engineering, Computer Science, Operations Research, or related discipline and 8–10 years of related experience, or 6–10 years with a Master’s degree. Additional experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
  • Demonstrated experience developing enterprise and mission architectures in UAF/UAFML (UAF 1.2 or later) in Cameo Enterprise Architecture or CATIA Magic, including multi-domain traceability across the UAF grid and integration with SysML system models.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting or directly supporting mission engineering studies, including mission characterization, mission thread and mission engineering thread development, mission metric definition, and analysis of alternative mission architectures.
  • Working knowledge of the DoW Mission Engineering Guide v2.0, DoWI 5000.88 (Engineering of Defense Systems), and DoWI 5000.97 (Digital Engineering), and their application to acquisition and capability development decisions.
  • Modeling and simulation experience using tools such as AFSIM, MATLAB/Simulink, or Ansys STK, including scenario development, execution, and analysis of results.
  • OMG Certified Systems Modeling Professional (OCSMP) Model Builder.
  • Experience supporting complex federal IT, systems engineering, or modernization programs, and familiarity with systems engineering lifecycle and requirements management practices.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • U.S. Citizenship required; ability to obtain and maintain a DHS Public Trust.

Preferred Qualifications

  • OMG Certified UAF Professional (OCUP or UAF certification) and experience with DoWAF-to-UAF migration or DoWAF view generation from UAF models.
  • Experience integrating UAF/SysML mission architectures with AFSIM or Ansys STK scenarios to trace mission outcomes back to system requirements and design decisions.
  • Experience supporting OUSD(R&E) mission engineering activities, Service mission engineering organizations, or experimentation campaigns tied to Key Operational Problems or equivalent Service-level priority operational problems.
  • Familiarity with SysML v2, its API and services, and model interoperability approaches for integrating architecture models with analysis and simulation tools.
  • Proficiency in Python or MATLAB for simulation automation, model queries, and data analysis; familiarity with operations research methods (design of experiments, sensitivity analysis) and HLA/DIS or cloud-based simulation environments.
  • Experience supporting U.S. Coast Guard, DHS, or DoW mission engineering, wargaming, or analytical modeling and simulation programs.
  • INCOSE CSEP/ESEP, DAU or Service mission engineering coursework, or Ansys STK / AFSIM training.

Please be advised that during the interview, you will be required to keep your camera on, and your interviewer will be taking your picture for identification purposes if an offer letter is extended to you.

We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.
